newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds France late to fully implement VAT rules.
newsitem.headline: Court finds France late to fully implement VAT rules.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday France failed to fully implement the VAT directive by continuing to provide a tax exemption on rented movable property.
The VAT directive requires VAT to be collected on the supply of services, but exempts the leasing or letting of certain immovable property.

Although French law taxes the supply of services, it permits a VAT exemption on residentital premises, which includes some mobile homes, touring caravans, tents, and light-framed leisure dwellings if they are characterized as genuine fixed residential installations.
The court accepted the European Commission's view that the French law goes beyond the VAT exemption which applies solely to the letting of immovable property.
In communications between the Commission and France, the French government agreed to change national laws and to tax the letting of tents, caravans or mobile homes.

The court has charged France with a failure to fulfil its obligations because the national rules were not officially changed by 1 January 1996, the date on which the period laid down in the Commission's reasoned opinion had expired.

Declares that, by introducing and maintaining in force an administrative provision extending to the letting of certain forms of movable property the exemption from VAT which, pursuant to article 13B(b) of the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) on the harmonization of the laws of member states relating to turnover taxes - Common basis of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment, is restricted exclusively to the letting of immovable property, the French Republic has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 2 of that directive
2. Orders the French Republic to pay the costs.
